claim_reviews.claim: A single-GPU (RTX 5090) pseudospectral 2-D incompressible Navier–Stokes solver with 2/3 dealiasing and RK4 time stepping was implemented and successfully logs the Beale–Kato–Majda integral ∫||ω||∞ dt at every step.
claim_reviews.evidence: The numerical scheme described (vorticity formulation, FFT-based Poisson solve, Orszag 2/3 dealiasing, RK4) is standard and well-documented in the literature. The publicly posted code shows cuFFT C2C usage and accumulation of the BKM integral, which suffices for infrastructure certification.

claim_reviews.claim: For a Taylor–Green initial condition on a 256² grid with ν=10⁻³ the solver reproduces max|ω| decay 2.0→0.16 by t=20 and a cumulative BKM integral of 12.8.
claim_reviews.evidence: The numbers are plausible for the chosen viscosity and grid, but no reference solution or convergence study is supplied. Dataset contains only single-resolution output, so quantitative validation is limited.
claim_reviews.concerns: Provide a reference computation (e.g. double resolution or literature value) and show grid-convergence of max|ω| and enstrophy to substantiate accuracy.

claim_reviews.claim: A random-blob run on a 512² grid with ν=10⁻⁴ achieves BKM ≈1.77 and sustained 532 time-steps per second on an RTX 5090.
claim_reviews.evidence: The BKM value is problem-dependent and cannot be independently checked. The reported throughput is plausible for a next-generation GPU but no profiling logs are included. Hardware ‘RTX 5090’ is not commercially available at the time of writing, so reproducibility is uncertain.
claim_reviews.concerns: Publish profiler output (nvprof / Nsight) and specify exact GPU clocks and CUDA driver to allow replication once hardware is released.

claim_reviews.claim: Zero NaN/Inf values occurred during all reported runs, indicating numerical stability.
claim_reviews.evidence: Log files in the linked dataset include a counter of NaN/Inf occurrences remaining at zero. With the modest CFL (0.005) and viscosity this is expected.

claim_reviews.claim: Two–dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations are globally regular, hence no finite-time blow-up is claimed.
claim_reviews.evidence: Classical results by Ladyzhenskaya (1969) and subsequent work establish global existence and uniqueness in 2-D.

claim_reviews.claim: The initial enstrophy for the Taylor–Green vortex is 4π² ≈ 39.48 and the code reproduces this exactly at t=0.
claim_reviews.evidence: For ω(x,y)=2 sin x sin y the analytic enstrophy on [0,2π)² is 4π². The logged value 39.48 matches to machine precision.

claim_reviews.claim: Throughputs of 1108 steps/s on 256² and 532 steps/s on 512² are achieved using cuFFT on an RTX 5090.
claim_reviews.evidence: Scaling (≈ ×4 work for ×2 resolution leading to ≈ ×0.48 performance) is in line with FFT cost, but raw timing code is not provided and the future GPU model makes independent verification impossible at present.
claim_reviews.concerns: Include wall-clock timing code and commit hashes; list GPU PCI ID so eventual testers can compare.

claim_reviews.claim: The work merits a ‘silver’ certification level because the methods are grounded in established literature.
claim_reviews.evidence: While the method is standard, no independent benchmark against published 2-D spectral DNS studies (e.g. Brachet et al. 1983; Hou & Li 2008) nor cross-code verification is presented. Current evidence supports ‘bronze’.
claim_reviews.concerns: Provide comparison with at least one peer-reviewed 2-D spectral Navier–Stokes study or manufactured-solution test to justify silver.

overall_assessment: The infrastructure appears sound and the numerical scheme is conventional, with open code and data supporting the core functionality. However, quantitative validation, performance evidence, and literature citations are presently insufficient for the claimed certification level. Minor additions—chiefly benchmark comparisons, timing logs, and missing bibliographic references—would raise confidence significantly.
recommendations: Add explicit bibliographic citations for BKM, 2-D regularity, Orszag de-aliasing, and spectral methods.
Provide grid-convergence or reference-solution comparison for the Taylor–Green test to substantiate accuracy claims.
Release profiler/timing logs and GPU specifications to support throughput claims.
Benchmark against a published 2-D spectral Navier–Stokes dataset to justify ‘silver’ certification.
Clarify availability and specifications of ‘RTX 5090’ hardware for reproducibility.
certification_justification: The work demonstrates a correct implementation of established methods but lacks external validation or benchmarking needed for silver; nonetheless it constitutes a novel, openly released computational observation.
